Then reason: The question says that on New Year's Day the a latitude line just has the phenomenon of polar night, indicating that a is the boundary latitude line of the polar-night range in the Northern Hemisphere on that day. New Year's Day is about 10 days from the winter solstice, and the direct solar point has moved northward by about 2.5° from about 23.5°S, so on New Year's Day the direct solar point is about at 21°S. The boundary latitude of polar night is approximately 90°−the absolute value of the latitude of the direct solar point, that is, 90°−21°≈69°. Since polar night on New Year's Day occurs in the Northern Hemisphere, the a latitude line is approximately 69°N.
